text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Manchester United get their 2023-24 campaign under way against Wolves at Old Trafford!

Erik ten Hag enters his second season in the Old Trafford dugout, looking to build on an encouraging 2022-23 campaign, which brought a third-placed Premier League finish and an end to United's six-year trophy drought.

While the club's takeover saga rumbles on and discontent with the Glazers' ownership remains, the signings of Andre Onana, Mason Mount and Rasmus Hojlund have lifted the mood at Old Trafford – can the Red Devils maintain that by starting the season strongly?

Wolves, meanwhile, have endured a less-than-ideal pre-season, with big-name players including Ruben Neves moving on and a lack of incomings causing Julen Lopetegui to quit as head coach on the eve of the new campaign.
Former Bournemouth boss Gary O'Neil oversees his first game at the helm here, knowing a positive performance is required after a difficult few weeks at Molineux.
Ten Hag hands full debuts to new recruits Onana and Mount, though Hojlund is expected to miss the first few weeks of the campaign.
As a result, Rashford appears likely to play centrally with Garnacho and Antony out wide.
Amid interest from West Ham, meanwhile, both Maguire and McTominay are named on the bench.
There are no new faces in the Wolves lineup, with the returning Doherty named among the substitutes.
Gomes and Lemina will have to step up in midfield following the departure of club captain Neves, while Sarabia, Matheus and Neto will hope to provide the creativity.
Cunha gets the nod up front, with Silva and Kalajdzic among O'Neil's options on the bench.
United are unbeaten in their last 18 Premier League home games (W15 D3), with their last defeat on this ground coming on the opening matchday against Brighton and Hove Albion 12 months ago.
Can Wolves shock the Old Trafford crowd? The teams are out, and kick-off is moments away.
We're under way for the 2023-24 season at Old Trafford as Fernandes gets the ball rolling for United!
A loose United pass almost allows Neto in, but Garnacho gets back to steal possession before getting United moving forwards.
Wolves attack for the first time as Semedo sees a shot deflect towards the corner flag.
Sarabia lets it run out of play, thinking it came off a red shirt last, but the referee points for a United goal-kick.
We're seeing two sides with very different aims here.
While United's fans are desperate to see them close the gap to rivals Manchester City, most Wolves supporters would surely take a repeat of last term's 13th-placed finish after a chaotic few months.
A heavy challenge from Sarabia catches Garnacho, and United win a free-kick.
Mount looks to dart onto Casemiro's pass following the set-piece, and Kilman clears behind for a corner.
Mount's delivery is punched clear by Sa, before the referee blows for a foul on a Wolves defender.
Antony drives inside to find Garnacho, but Lemina is on hand to make a fine challenge on the edge of his own box as Wolves clear the danger.
No team has won their opening Premier League game more often than Manchester United (20), though the Red Devils have started two of the last three campaigns with a loss.
They lost at home to Brighton in their first game of last season, and last lost their opening league game in consecutive campaigns in 1972-73 and 1973-74.
Action at both ends as Sarabia's cutback is cleared ahead of Neto, and United's subsequent break is stopped by Cunha, who races back to stop Garnacho's advance.
Good save! United create the first real opening as Rashford darts in behind, but Sa closes the angle and smothers his shot from the right-hand side of the box.
That's better from United after a slow start from the hosts.
Good strength from Wan-Bissaka to stop Cunha darting in behind.
Antony is then dragged down by Ait-Nouri on halfway, and the Wolves left-back is fortunate to escape a yellow card.
O'Neil will be relatively pleased with Wolves' start.
United have yet to get going and the visitors have almost caught them out on the break on a couple of occasions.
Garnacho looks to find Fernandes in the final third, but Dawson steps out to make a vital interception.
He read that situation brilliantly.
Martinez scythes Neto down as the Portugal winger looks to break clear down the left, and the United defender picks up a deserved yellow card.
Nothing comes of the free-kick, but the Red Devils man is walking a tightrope now.
Wolves have lost their opening league game in each of the last two seasons.
They are looking to avoid starting three consecutive campaigns with a defeat, which they last did between 1988-89 and 1990-91.
Wonderful feet from Ait-Nouri, who beats Casemiro and Mount to enter United's half.
He then finds Cunha, but the Brazilian is outmuscled by his compatriot Casemiro.
Rashford's four touches is the fewest of any player on the pitch so far.
United are struggling to provide their talisman with service.
Garnacho finds Shaw with a neat backheel inside the box, but Semedo gets back to cover.
A deep cross then almost finds Antony at the second time of asking, but Matheus gets back to clear the danger.
Great defending! Fernandes dispossesses Gomes and looks to thread a dangerous throughball into the box, but Wolves right-back Semedo chases back to make a crucial interception.
CLOSE! Cunha beats Casemiro and Martinez with ease on the break before finding Sarabia, who sees his low drive deflect narrowly wide of the bottom-right corner.
Dawson heads down the resulting corner, but United clear at the second time of asking.
Wolves are asking questions of their hosts.
Lemina sees a shot blocked outside the area before cynically dragging Fernandes down to stop a United break.
He becomes the first visiting player to enter the book.
We've passed the half-hour mark at Old Trafford, and though United are enjoying a lot of possession, they're yet to seriously test Sa.
Wolves have been combative in midfield and lively on the break.
Ait-Nouri breaks forward to win a throw-in on the left, before Casemiro escapes punishment after catching Cunha.
The United midfielder was extremely fortunate not to concede the foul.
JUST WIDE! Wolves are really threatening on the break! Sarabia slips it through for Cunha, who drags his shot narrowly wide of the bottom-left corner.
The Old Trafford crowd is growing restless.
Wolves are winless in their last eight Premier League away games (D2 L6), losing the last four in a row by an aggregate score of 15-1.
They've shown plenty of purpose in the opening 35 minutes here, however.
Officials have been told to come down harshly on timewasting this season, and Ait-Nouri goes into the book for delaying the restart over a throw-in.
Scramble! Shaw gets up on the overlap and his cross is spilled by Sa.
Garnacho and Fernandes try to turn it home only for Kilman to block near the line, but the referee eventually blows for a foul by Garnacho.
Rashford appeals for handball after heading Wan-Bissaka's cross against Semedo, but the defender's arm is in a totally natural position.
United were never getting a penalty for that – the VAR check is swiftly complete.
Cunha breaks into the box but is denied by a wonderful challenge from Wan-Bissaka, who slides in to kick the ball off the Wolves man and out, winning a goal-kick.
United are starting to penalty Wolves back a little more now, but they're lacking fluidity in midfield.
Casemiro and Mount are operating as a double pivot with Fernandes supporting Rashford, but Wolves' backline is proving difficult to breach.
Rashford is crowded out in the area before Garnacho flashes a powerful effort well wide from a tight angle on the left.
Neto capitalises on Sarabia's hold-up play to beat four United challenges and reach the area, but Martinez eventually gets a foot in to deny Wolves a shot at goal.
Shaw scythed Sarabia down earlier in that move, and though the referee initially played advantage, he now goes back to book the full-back.
That was another promising counterattack from Wolves, but they failed to make it count.
We're into two minutes of stoppage time at the end of this opening period.
Unlike others across the Premier League's opening matchday, this game has flowed very nicely.

Wolves almost play themselves into trouble! A loose pass allows Rashford to break in behind, but newly-appointed skipper Kilman matches him stride-for-stride to make a last-ditch challenge, conceding a corner.
Wide! Mount's delivery is good, but Varane sends an awkward header wide at the back post.
The Frenchman was just stretching for that, and he failed to make a strong connection.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-0 WOLVES.
Simon Hooper blows the half-time whistle and it remains goalless between Manchester United and Wolves.
Despite all the pre-match noise, the visitors have given as good as they've got here, with Cunha and Sarabia both going close to finding the bottom corner on the break.
O'Neil will be delighted with Wolves' tenacity and organisation, with Sa's routine save to deny Rashford the closest United have come to an opener.
Ten Hag will demand much more after the interval.
Despite enjoying over 60 per cent of the possession, United have managed just one shot on target and 16 touches inside the Wolves area.
The Red Devils have looked very disjointed so far, and there is surely more to come in the second half.
Ten Hag makes a half-time substitution as Lindelof replaces Martinez.
The Argentine was booked early on and has looked nervous throughout, so that change makes sense for United.
Wolves kick off for the second half at Old Trafford.
Can either team find a winner?
Neto beats Shaw for pace and reaches the byline, where his cutback is smothered behind by Onana.
Sarabia floats the corner in, but United stand firm to clear their lines.
Lindelof's half-time introduction is surely more evidence, if it was needed, that Maguire's United career is over.
The displaced captain continues to watch on from the bench, as rumours swirl that he could be joining David Moyes' West Ham soon.
CUNHA HITS THE POST! What a let-off for United! Matheus charges forward from his own half before picking out Sarabia.
His low cross finds its way to Cunha at the far post, but with Onana stranded, the Brazilian side-foots against the post and behind.
Wolves should be 1-0 up!
The Old Trafford crowd is trying to rouse their team as Sa mops up a ball in behind.
Wolves have squandered some glorious chances here – will they live to regret them?
OFF THE LINE! Garnacho reaches a ball down the channel and beats the stranded Sa with a delicate lob.
It looks to be dropping beneath the crossbar, but Dawson gets back to head it over his own crossbar.
Great defending!
Almost an own goal! Kilman almost turns a left-wing cross into his own net as United continue to press, but Sa is well-placed to hold onto it.
This is better from the hosts.

Good save from Onana! Cunha is still getting plenty of joy on the break! Another fine run takes the Brazilian through the heart of midfield, before his 25-yard effort is turned around the post by Onana! That's another warning for the Red Devils.
Wolves' corner comes to nothing, but they keep the pressure on and Neto wins another set-piece by blasting the ball into Shaw's face and behind.
The left-back receives treatment before being given the all-clear to continue.
Wolves' corner almost finds Dawson at the back post, but United nervously clear the lines.
The hosts break through Rashford, and Garnacho eventually blasts a long-range effort over the crossbar.
Garnacho wins a corner on the right for United, from which Fernandes goes short to the Argentine.
He steps inside and blasts a wild effort all the way through the box and wide.
Wolves are about to turn to their bench for the first time.
Hwang is receiving instructions and will enter the fray imminently.
We're past the hour-mark and O'Neil's men are still holding their own.
Hwang takes Sarabia's place alongside Cunha in the Wolves attack.
Hwang's first involvement sees him hold up the ball near the touchline before being wiped out by Wan-Bissaka.
The right-back is fortunate to escape a yellow card, but United will have to defend a wide free-kick from the Wolves left.
Neto's delivery finds Cunha, but he gets his header all wrong and sends it bouncing well wide of Onana's goal.
Having gone unbeaten in their first four Premier League meetings with United following their return to the top flight in 2018 (W1 D3), Wolves have lost five of their last six against the Red Devils.
They've performed admirably so far here – can they go on to claim a point, or perhaps all three?
Wolves have created plenty of promising situations on the break here.
Ait-Nouri is the latest to charge through the middle of the park, but Varane cuts out his cross before Hwang sends a wild effort off-target.
United are making a double change as they chase a winner.
Eriksen replaces Mount, who has endured a difficult Red Devils debut.
Sancho, meanwhile, is on for Garnacho.
Neto is frustrated by the decision to award United a throw-in inside their own half, and the winger picks up a yellow card for delaying the restart.
Hwang and Matheus link up on the break before the former finds Neto in space on the right.
His deep cross is carried behind by Onana, and Wolves win a corner, much to the crowd's frustration.
Varane heads the corner away, but Wolves keep the attack alive and will come again.
WHAT A CHANCE! Another outstanding run from Cunha sees the Brazilian feed Hwang, whose cutback deflects into the path of Neto.
He has time to pick his spot from 12 yards out, but his shot is straight at Onana.
Wolves should really be ahead here!
Sancho is involved for the first time as he cuts inside and wins a corner off Gomes.
Shaw's kick is cleared by the first defender, and Cunha is on hand to stop Sancho's second delivery.
GOOAAAAL! VARANE PUTS UNITED AHEAD! Wolves are made to pay for their missed chances as Varane nods in from close range.
Fernandes lifts a delicate ball over the Wolves backline, and Wan-Bissaka's volleyed cross is headed in by Varane from inside the six-yard box! 1-0!
Wan-Bissaka gets the assist after lifting a fine cross onto Varane's head, but Fernandes deserves plenty of credit for unlocking the Wolves defence with a fine ball over the top.
United make another change despite taking the lead as Pellistri replaces Antony.
O'Neil, meanwhile, responds to that setback with two changes of his own.
Bueno replaces Ait-Nouri at left-back.
Cunha, meanwhile, is replaced by Silva up front.
O'Neil will be wondering how his side have found themselves behind here.
They've created chance after chance but have been hit by a real sucker punch from Varane.
They have 11 minutes plus stoppage time to respond.
Hwang chests down a cross from the right, but he's off-balance as he volleys towards goal and steers his effort well wide.
Varane's goal was just his second in the Premier League and his first in 26 appearances in the competition, since he netted against Brentford in May 2022.
SAVE! Matheus gets to the byline and sees his cutback deflect off Shaw before dropping to Silva.
The substitute blasts at goal from a tight angle, but Onana stands firm to push it behind.
WOLVES GO CLOSE AGAIN! Gomes does brilliantly to reach Silva's flick-on before teeing up the striker 10 yards out.
He sends another low drive towards goal, but Onana reacts to save with his feet.
Wolves are continuing to cause problems.
The Old Trafford crowd is growing nervous.
Despite going ahead, United have exerted no control over this game and are continuing to concede chances.
Only Wolves' poor finishing has kept the score at 1-0.
United are attempting to hold onto what they have now.
McTominay is on for Rashford, who has been quiet.
Wolves, meanwhile, bring on towering striker Kalajdzic for Gomes in an attacking switch.
Wolves win a free-kick 25 yards from goal, slightly to the right of the box, which Matheus lifts in.
Kalajdzic meets it, but his header loops into Onana's hands.
Wolves are running out of time to find a leveller.
It just won't happen for Wolves! Hwang races in behind to tee up Silva, who shoots on the turn but sees his effort blocked by Lindelof.
United are clinging on.
We will have a minimum of SEVEN additional minutes here.
Can United hold on?
Wolves have had 18 shots to United's 15 in this game, managing six attempts on target to the hosts' three.
Still, the Red Devils lead.
CLOSE TO 1-1! Silva finds Hwang in an inside-left position, and the South Korea international beats Wan-Bissaka before firing at goal.
The right-back recovers brilliantly, however, to make a goal-saving challenge inside his own area.
Wolves continue to pepper the United goal with shots as Silva and Lemina see efforts blocked at close range.
United are living very dangerously now.
PENALTY APPEAL! Onana charges from his line as Kalajdzic attacks a right-wing cross, and the United goalkeeper completely misses the ball with his punch, taking out the Wolves player instead.
That was totally reckless from the United new-boy, and the VAR will take a closer look!
CONTROVERSY! NO PENALTY IS THE DECISION! Wow.
Onana is very lucky.
The VAR check is complete, and Wolves are denied a spot-kick.
O'Neil is absolutely seething, and he receives a yellow card for his protests.
Wolves continue to press as Neto hangs up a cross, but Onana holds it at the second attempt.
Wolves have been desperately unlucky here, but United have surely done enough now.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-0 WOLVES.
The referee blows for full-time, and United cling on to start their season with a win.
Varane's goal was the difference, the defender nodding in from close range after good work from Fernandes and Wan-Bissaka.
Wolves will feel they did enough to win this game, with Cunha hitting the post, Neto and Silva squandering good chances, and a VAR review denying them a penalty at the death.
Despite the result, O'Neil will be very encouraged by Wolves' display.
Wolves finish the game with 23 shots to United's 15 and 2.23 xG to the hosts' 1.46.
They will be hopeful of picking up results if they continue to play in this manner, with Brighton and Hove Albion their next opponents at Molineux on Saturday.
United, meanwhile, go to Tottenham for a huge test on the same day.
We hope you have enjoyed our coverage of this clash at Old Trafford.
Thank you for joining us, and we'll see you next time.
